title: Contract fuzzing harness and canary health scorer for structured-output/toolcall changes
creator: Asha Menon
description: Problem: During model upgrades that change structured output (function-call shapes, JSON contracts), subtle incompatibilities slip through canaries and shadow traffic because existing diffing is brittle and sensitive to benign ordering/whitespace or unrelated optional fields. This ticket builds a repeatable, automated contract-fuzzing harness (input perturbations + schema-aware mutations) and a canary health scorer that aggregates behavioral and schema signals into a single canary health metric used by rollout automation for auto-rollback decisions.
acceptance_criteria: A contract-fuzzing job can generate 10k diverse structured-output call events for any model variant given a canonical schema and seed prompts
A canary health scorer returns a normalized 0..100 health score combining schema-compatibility, function-call signature diffs, semantic output regressions, and latency/error signals
Automation: rollout controller uses health score thresholds to mark canary as PASS/WARN/FAIL and triggers auto-unwind on FAIL based on documented playbook
Dashboards: per-canary telemetry (schema violation rate, avg health score, top diffs) available in Console and linked from rollout UI
Guardrails: false-positive rate of schema detection reviewed with PM/SDK team and documented fallback path for noisy features
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (schema-fuzz harness): implement fuzzing primitives that mutate optional/extra fields, reorder keys, inject nulls/empty arrays, and alter types in a schema-aware manner
Phase 2 (diff normalization): build a canonicalizer that normalizes ordering, strips insignificant whitespace, and canonicalizes timestamps/IDs before diffing

Phase 3 (health scorer): define signals and weights (schema_violation_rate 40%, required_field_mismatch 25%, semantic_delta_score 20%, error_rate 10%, latency_penalty 5%) and implement aggregator service
Phase 4 (integration): wire harness and scorer into canary pipeline: shadow traffic -> fuzzed probes -> scorer -> rollout controller decision
Phase 5 (automation + rollback playbook): implement controller thresholds and an auto-unwind action that re-routes traffic and creates a linked incident + postmortem checklist
risk_considerations: Fuzzer may surface non-actionable differences (order-only or stable random fields) — mitigated by canonicalizer and allowlist rules
Scorer weights may need tuning per-customer or per-model family; expose as config in rollout policy
Performance cost: fuzzing across many permutations is expensive — we will limit to prioritized probes and sample sizes during live canaries
False auto-rollbacks could be disruptive: initial rollout will only create WARN events for 24h before enabling auto-unwind in production
rollout_plan: Start with internal canaries (platform team) in staged environments using internal-only models
Enable shadow traffic + fuzz probes at 0.5% traffic for first week, collect metrics
Tune canonicalizer rules and scorer weights with PM and SDK feedback
Open beta: opt-in customers can enable extended checks for a month
Enable auto-unwind once system maintains <2% false-positive WARN->FAILs over 2 consecutive cycles

open_questions: What is the canonical definition of 'semantic_delta_score' and which eval harness should provide it? (action: pair with evals team)
Should scorer be per-model-family or globally weighted? (trade-off: per-model yields less noise but more config surface)
How do we safely expose expanded checks to customers without overwhelming support? (action: staged opt-in and clear UI explanations)
What constitutes an explicit exception/compatibility shim vs. a genuine regression that must be auto-unwound?
